disposition_reason: Table 3 gives regional mean ± SD for 18 elements including Cd, Ni, Cr, Co in 138 single origin chocolates, and the text lists individual Pb and Cd values for exceeding samples.

study.design: market survey of single origin dark and milk chocolates with multi-element fingerprinting
study.origin: cacao origin per packaging: Africa, Asia Pacific, Central America, South America (27 countries)
study.market: purchased online and in retail in Belgium (86), Colombia (3), Ecuador (25), France (10), Italy (3), Madagascar (6), Mexico (2), New Zealand (2), Peru (1), Switzerland (1)
study.method: ICP-MS (Agilent 7700x, collision cell) after open-block HNO3 digestion, 11 h at 130 C
study.lod_text: LOQ (10 SD of 4 procedural blanks): Cd 0.01, Pb 0.02, As 0.08, Ni 0.16, Cr 0.04, Co 0.01 mg/kg (Table 3; text)
study.qa: NIST 2384 baking chocolate and ERM-BD512 dark chocolate in triplicate per batch; recoveries 79-102% (Table S1, not in the PDF); Fe excluded for poor recovery; duplicate CV 1-23%

Macro elements Ca, K, Mg, P, S in Table 3 not extracted (nutrients).
Chocolate type (dark vs milk) is not reported per sample; cacao content ranged 32-100%.
Pb listed sample 0.10 mg/kg equals rather than exceeds the stated 0.10 limit, though the authors count it among six exceedances.
